name: EU Consumer Rights Directive (2011/83/EU)
description: Statutory rules covering EU CRD 2011/83/EU prohibitions on pre-ticked subscription boxes and requirements for transparent cancellation mechanisms.

rules.title: Pre-Ticked Consent Box & Default Subscription Enrollment

statute.title: Prohibition of Pre-Ticked Default Options
statute.plainExplanation: EU law strictly prohibits traders from inferring consumer consent through pre-ticked checkboxes or default selections for recurring payments.

rules.explanation: The terms or checkout flow indicate that a recurring subscription option or add-on fee is selected or checked by default.
rules.recommendation: EU Directive 2011/83/EU bans pre-ticked boxes across all EU member states. Subscription consent must be an explicit affirmative opt-in.

rules.title: Statutory 14-Day EU Withdrawal Right Waiver

statute.title: Unwaivable Right of Withdrawal
statute.plainExplanation: EU consumers possess a statutory 14-day right of withdrawal from distance and digital subscription contracts that cannot be waived or contracted away.

rules.explanation: The clause purports to waive, forfeit, or exclude your statutory 14-day EU right of withdrawal upon starting a subscription.
rules.recommendation: Under Directive 2011/83/EU Article 25, contractual clauses derogating from consumer withdrawal rights are null and void across the European Union.

rules.title: Bundled Subscription & Tracking/Profiling Consent

statute.title: Unbundled Freely-Given Consent Mandate
statute.plainExplanation: Consent to behavioral advertising or profiling cannot be bundled into acceptance of subscription terms as a condition of service.

rules.explanation: The subscription contract conditions service access on blanket acceptance of behavioral tracking, advertising cookies, or automated profiling.
rules.recommendation: GDPR Article 7 requires data processing consent to be freely given, specific, and unbundled from subscription contract performance.
